# Introduction

This article adds a third data source to the
[Delhi PM2.5 Analysis (2022)](delhi_pm2.5_analysis.html). The third source is the
OAQ (Open Air Quality) platform. OAQ collects real-time sensor readings from CPCB
reference stations. Its pollutant coverage is much larger than the coverage of
the historical CPCB data repository.

The original analysis used the historical CPCB data repository (daily
city/station-level PM2.5 CSVs) and WUSTL ACAG satellite data. Its question was:
*where in Delhi are monitoring gaps largest?* This article adds two new
questions:

> **Q1:** Does the full multi-pollutant OAQ data change our understanding of the
> current monitoring network in Delhi, compared with PM2.5 alone?

> **Q2:** When we add the OAQ CPCB stations, does the result of the monitoring
> gap analysis change? These stations have more pollutant metadata, and their
> coordinates come directly from the platform.

The primary difference is that OAQ supplies live, multi-pollutant readings
(PM2.5, PM10, NO2, CO, O3, NOx) through the `oaq_get_stations_latest()`
endpoint. The data includes the station coordinates, so a geocoding step is not
necessary.

---

# Data sources

| Source | Access function | What it provides |
|---|---|---|
| CPCB historical | `cpcb_download_city_data()` | Daily city-level PM2.5 (2022) |
| WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 | `pm25_get_stats()` | Satellite PM2.5 rasters (2022) |
| OAQ platform | `oaq_session()` + `oaq_get_stations_latest()` | Live multi-pollutant readings + coords |

# Baseline reproduction (historical CPCB + satellite)

We reproduce the seasonal trend and the ward-level choropleth from the original
article. Thus, you can compare the two analyses directly. If you ran the
original article before, this article uses its cached CSV files again.

```{r delhi-shape}
delhi_shape <- sf::st_read(
  "https://geo.bharatviz.org/geojsons/cities/delhi.geojson",
  quiet = TRUE
) %>% sf::st_make_valid()
```

```{r ground-data}
delhi_ground <- cpcb_city_daily("Delhi", 2022, cache_dir = data_dir) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(ground_pm25 = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r satellite-data}
delhi_sat_df <- pm25_monthly(delhi_shape, 2022, version = "V5GL04", region = "AS", cache_dir = nc_dir) %>%
  rename(sat_pm25 = pm25)

delhi_final <- inner_join(delhi_ground, delhi_sat_df, by = "month")
```

```{r raster-nov}
nov_file <- pm25_download_netcdf(2022, 11, version = "V5GL04", region = "AS", cache_dir = nc_dir)
r_nov <- pm25_load_netcdf_bbox(nov_file, delhi_shape)
delhi_raster_mask <- pm25_load_netcdf_bbox(nov_file, delhi_shape, mask = TRUE)
```

```{r ward-pm25}
delhi_wards <- delhi_shape
delhi_wards$sat_pm25 <- exactextractr::exact_extract(
  r_nov, delhi_wards, "mean",
  progress = FALSE
)
```

---

# OAQ station data

## Connect to the OAQ platform

The OAQ API uses a 2-step handshake. First, a call to the Data Broker with your
API key gets a signed session. Then, all data requests include that signature.
You can give the API key directly or through the `OAQ_API_KEY` environment
variable.

```{r oaq-session}
session <- oaq_session()
```

## Get the Delhi stations from OAQ

`oaq_get_stations_latest()` returns the most recent reading for all stations of
a provider. The `"cpcb"` provider includes all 46 Delhi CAAQMS stations, with
full pollutant coverage. The data includes the coordinates, so geocoding is not
necessary.

```{r oaq-stations}
oaq_delhi <- oaq_stations_table(session, "cpcb") %>%
  filter(city %in% c("Delhi", "New Delhi"))

cat(nrow(oaq_delhi), "OAQ CPCB stations in Delhi\n")
cat("PM2.5 available for:", sum(!is.na(oaq_delhi$pm25)), "stations\n")
cat("NO2  available for:", sum(!is.na(oaq_delhi$no2)), "stations\n")
cat("O3   available for:", sum(!is.na(oaq_delhi$o3)), "stations\n")
```

```{r oaq-sf}
oaq_delhi_sf <- oaq_delhi %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326)
```

## Live pollutant snapshot

The OAQ platform has data for more pollutants than the historical CPCB CSVs.
The table below is a summary of the current readings for all active Delhi
stations.

```{r pollutant-summary}
oaq_delhi %>%
  select(name, city, pm25, pm10, no2, o3, co, nox) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(pm25, pm10, no2, o3, co, nox),
    names_to = "pollutant", values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  group_by(pollutant) %>%
  summarise(
    n_stations = n(),
    mean       = round(mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    median     = round(median(value, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    min        = round(min(value, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    max        = round(max(value, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    .groups    = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(pollutant)
```

# Station network comparison

## Historical CPCB vs OAQ coverage

In the original article, the historical CPCB analysis got the station
coordinates from `cpcb_add_coords()`. This function queries the CPCB live feed
and uses Nominatim as a fallback. OAQ supplies the coordinates directly in its
response. We compare the two networks to find differences.

```{r cpcb-stations}
station_file <- file.path(data_dir, "delhi_stations_with_coords.csv")
if (file.exists(station_file)) {
  delhi_station_list <- read.csv(station_file)
} else {
  delhi_station_list <- cpcb_add_coords(cpcb_get_station_list("Delhi"))
  write.csv(delhi_station_list, station_file, row.names = FALSE)
}

cpcb_sf <- delhi_station_list %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon)) %>%
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
  mutate(source = "CPCB historical")

oaq_compare_sf <- oaq_delhi_sf %>%
  mutate(source = "OAQ live")
```

```{r network-comparison, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Station network comparison: CPCB historical (from cpcb_add_coords) vs OAQ live platform. Both sources cover the same 46 stations. OAQ coordinates come directly from the platform, without geocoding."}
delhi_boundary <- sf::st_union(delhi_shape)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data      = delhi_boundary,
    fill      = "grey97",
    color     = "grey60",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = cpcb_sf,
    aes(color = source),
    size = 3,
    shape = 16,
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = oaq_compare_sf,
    aes(color = source),
    size = 2,
    shape = 17,
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "CPCB historical" = "#d77027ff",
      "OAQ live"        = "#4575b4"
    ),
    name = "Data source"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Delhi CAAQMS: CPCB historical vs OAQ live station locations",
    subtitle = "Circles = CPCB historical (cpcb_add_coords) | Triangles = OAQ live platform\nBoth cover the same 46 stations. OAQ coordinates require no geocoding step",
    caption  = "Source: CPCB data repository + OAQ platform (oaq.notf.in)"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top",
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig_oaq1_network_comparison.png"), width = 9, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

# Multi-pollutant choropleth (OAQ)

The original article used satellite-derived PM2.5 to color the wards. In this
article, we use the live OAQ PM2.5 readings at each station. Each ward gets the
reading of its nearest station. The result is a ground-measured ward map that
adds to the satellite view.

```{r oaq-ward-pm25}
# For each ward centroid, find the nearest OAQ station and its live PM2.5
oaq_pm25_sf <- oaq_delhi_sf %>% filter(!is.na(pm25))
ward_centroids <- sf::st_centroid(delhi_wards)

dist_oaq <- sf::st_distance(ward_centroids, oaq_pm25_sf)
nearest_oaq_idx <- apply(dist_oaq, 1, which.min)

delhi_wards$oaq_pm25 <- oaq_pm25_sf$pm25[nearest_oaq_idx]
delhi_wards$oaq_dist_km <- apply(dist_oaq, 1, min) / 1000
delhi_wards$oaq_station <- oaq_pm25_sf$name[nearest_oaq_idx]
```

```{r oaq-choropleth, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Ward-level PM2.5 from the nearest OAQ station (live reading). Blue triangles are OAQ CPCB stations. The color shows the current reading at the nearest station."}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_wards,
    aes(fill = oaq_pm25),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data  = oaq_pm25_sf,
    color = "black",
    fill  = "#4575b4",
    size  = 2.5,
    shape = 24,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette = "YlOrRd",
    direction = 1,
    na.value = "grey80",
    name = expression(paste("OAQ PM"[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3)))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Delhi ward-level PM2.5: OAQ live readings",
    subtitle = "Ward shading = nearest OAQ station PM2.5 | Blue triangles = OAQ CPCB stations",
    caption = paste0(
      "Live data from OAQ platform (oaq.notf.in)\n",
      "Fetched: ", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M IST")
    )
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top",
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig_oaq2_ward_pm25_live.png"), width = 9, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

# Satellite vs OAQ ground

```{r sat-vs-oaq}
comparison_df <- delhi_wards %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(!is.na(sat_pm25), !is.na(oaq_pm25)) %>%
  mutate(delta_oaq = sat_pm25 - oaq_pm25)

cor_oaq <- cor(comparison_df$sat_pm25, comparison_df$oaq_pm25,
  use = "complete.obs"
)
cat("Correlation (satellite vs OAQ ground): r =", round(cor_oaq, 3), "\n")
cat("Mean satellite PM2.5:", round(mean(comparison_df$sat_pm25, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "\n")
cat("Mean OAQ ground PM2.5:", round(mean(comparison_df$oaq_pm25, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "\n")
```

```{r sat-oaq-scatter, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Satellite (WUSTL Nov 2022) vs OAQ live ground PM2.5 by ward. The satellite data is from November 2022. The OAQ readings are current. The time mismatch explains the variance that the point-to-area measurement difference does not explain."}
ggplot(comparison_df, aes(x = oaq_pm25, y = sat_pm25)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = oaq_dist_km), size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
    color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm", se = TRUE,
    color = "firebrick", fill = "pink", alpha = 0.2
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = max(comparison_df$oaq_pm25, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.55,
    y = max(comparison_df$sat_pm25, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.92,
    label = paste0("r = ", round(cor_oaq, 2)),
    size = 4.5, color = "grey20"
  ) +
  scale_color_distiller(
    palette   = "YlOrRd",
    direction = 1,
    name      = "Dist. to nearest\nOAQ station (km)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Satellite (Nov 2022) vs OAQ live ground PM2.5 by ward",
    subtitle = "Dashed line = 1:1 | Linear fit in red | Color = distance to nearest OAQ station",
    x        = expression(paste("OAQ live PM"[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3))),
    y        = expression(paste("Satellite PM"[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3) ~ "(Nov 2022)")),
    caption  = "Note: temporal mismatch (2022 satellite vs live readings) contributes to variance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "right",
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  )

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig_oaq3_sat_vs_oaq.png"), width = 9, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
```

# Updated gap analysis with OAQ stations

The original gap analysis used the CPCB historical station coordinates. We do
the analysis again with the OAQ station coordinates and compare the priority
maps. OAQ supplies the coordinates directly, without a Nominatim fallback. Thus,
OAQ is the more authoritative source of station locations.

```{r oaq-gap-analysis}
dist_matrix_oaq <- sf::st_distance(ward_centroids, oaq_pm25_sf)
nearest_oaq <- apply(dist_matrix_oaq, 1, which.min)

delhi_wards$nearest_oaq_km <- apply(dist_matrix_oaq, 1, min) / 1000
delhi_wards$nearest_oaq_pm25 <- oaq_pm25_sf$pm25[nearest_oaq]
delhi_wards$delta_oaq <- delhi_wards$sat_pm25 - delhi_wards$nearest_oaq_pm25

delhi_wards <- delhi_wards %>%
  mutate(
    priority_oaq = case_when(
      nearest_oaq_km > 2 &
        sat_pm25 > median(sat_pm25, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "High priority",
      nearest_oaq_km > 2 ~ "Medium priority",
      TRUE ~ "Well monitored"
    )
  )

cat("Priority breakdown (OAQ-based):\n")
print(table(delhi_wards$priority_oaq))
```

```{r oaq-gap-map, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Updated monitoring gap map with OAQ station coordinates. The ward color shows the satellite PM2.5 minus the live PM2.5 at the nearest OAQ station. Blue triangles are OAQ station locations."}
centroid_coords_oaq <- sf::st_coordinates(ward_centroids)
oaq_station_coords <- sf::st_coordinates(oaq_pm25_sf)[nearest_oaq, ]

connection_lines_oaq <- data.frame(
  x_from = centroid_coords_oaq[, 1],
  y_from = centroid_coords_oaq[, 2],
  x_to   = oaq_station_coords[, 1],
  y_to   = oaq_station_coords[, 2],
  delta  = delhi_wards$delta_oaq
) %>% filter(!is.na(delta))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_wards,
    aes(fill = delta_oaq),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.1
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = connection_lines_oaq,
    aes(x = x_from, y = y_from, xend = x_to, yend = y_to),
    color = "grey15", linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.5, linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data  = oaq_pm25_sf,
    color = "black",
    fill  = "#4575b4",
    size  = 2.5,
    shape = 24,
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = khroma::colour("roma")(100),
    values = scales::rescale(c(
      min(delhi_wards$delta_oaq, na.rm = TRUE),
      median(delhi_wards$delta_oaq, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(delhi_wards$delta_oaq, na.rm = TRUE)
    )),
    na.value = "grey80",
    name = expression(paste(Delta ~ PM[2.5] ~ (mu * g / m^3)))
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Delhi: satellite vs nearest OAQ station PM2.5 by ward",
    subtitle = "Dashed lines connect each ward centroid to its nearest OAQ station\nColor shows satellite − OAQ live reading | Blue triangles = OAQ stations",
    caption  = "Delta = satellite PM2.5 (Nov 2022) − nearest OAQ live reading\nSource: WUSTL ACAG V5GL04 + OAQ platform (oaq.notf.in)"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  coord_sf() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position  = "top",
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey40")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.6, "lines")
  ))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig_oaq4_gap_map_oaq.png"), width = 9, height = 7.5, dpi = 300)
```

## Priority map comparison

```{r priority-comparison, fig.height=7, fig.width=12, fig.cap="Priority map comparison: CPCB historical coordinates (left, from the original article) vs OAQ live coordinates (right). Differences between the maps show where the coordinate source changes the conclusions of the gap analysis."}
# Load original CPCB-based priority from the original analysis, if available
# (Recompute here for self-containedness)
cpcb_sf_pm25 <- cpcb_sf %>%
  left_join(
    delhi_station_list %>%
      select(value, label) %>%
      rename(id = value, name = label),
    by = c("label" = "name")
  )

dist_cpcb_orig <- sf::st_distance(ward_centroids, cpcb_sf)
nearest_cpcb <- apply(dist_cpcb_orig, 1, which.min)

delhi_wards$nearest_cpcb_km <- apply(dist_cpcb_orig, 1, min) / 1000
delhi_wards <- delhi_wards %>%
  mutate(
    priority_cpcb = case_when(
      nearest_cpcb_km > 2 &
        sat_pm25 > median(sat_pm25, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "High priority",
      nearest_cpcb_km > 2 ~ "Medium priority",
      TRUE ~ "Well monitored"
    )
  )

priority_colors <- c(
  "High priority"   = "#d6604d",
  "Medium priority" = "#fdae61",
  "Well monitored"  = "#4dac26"
)

p_cpcb <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_wards, aes(fill = priority_cpcb),
    color = "white", linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = cpcb_sf, color = "black", fill = "yellow",
    size = 2.5, shape = 21
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = priority_colors, na.value = "grey80",
    name = "Priority"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "CPCB historical coords",
    subtitle = "Circles = CPCB stations"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

p_oaq <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(
    data = delhi_wards, aes(fill = priority_oaq),
    color = "white", linewidth = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_sf(
    data = oaq_pm25_sf, color = "black", fill = "#4575b4",
    size = 2.5, shape = 24
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = priority_colors, na.value = "grey80",
    name = "Priority"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "OAQ live coords",
    subtitle = "Triangles = OAQ stations"
  ) +
  xlab(NULL) +
  ylab(NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

p_cpcb + p_oaq + patchwork::plot_layout(ncol = 2)
```

# Multi-pollutant station profile

An advantage of OAQ over the historical CPCB CSVs is data for many co-located
pollutants. The ranked bubble chart below shows the full pollutant profile for
the active Delhi stations.

```{r pollutant-profile, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Multi-pollutant profile for Delhi CPCB stations from OAQ. Each row is a station. Each column is a pollutant. Circle size and color show concentration. Gray shows a pollutant that the station does not measure, or a station that is offline."}
# Tidy to long format, normalise within each pollutant for colour scaling
oaq_long <- oaq_delhi %>%
  select(id, name, city, pm25, pm10, no2, o3, co, nox) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(pm25, pm10, no2, o3, co, nox),
    names_to = "pollutant", values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  # Normalise within each pollutant so different units are comparable visually
  group_by(pollutant) %>%
  mutate(value_norm = (value - min(value, na.rm = TRUE)) /
    (max(value, na.rm = TRUE) - min(value, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    pollutant = factor(pollutant,
      levels = c("pm25", "pm10", "no2", "o3", "co", "nox"),
      labels = c("PM2.5", "PM10", "NO₂", "O₃", "CO", "NOx")
    ),
    # Shorten station names for the axis
    name_short = stringr::str_remove(name, ", Delhi.*$") %>%
      stringr::str_remove(", New Delhi.*$") %>%
      stringr::str_trunc(30)
  )

station_order <- oaq_delhi %>%
  arrange(desc(pm25)) %>%
  pull(name) %>%
  {
    stringr::str_remove(., ", Delhi.*$")
  } %>%
  {
    stringr::str_remove(., ", New Delhi.*$")
  } %>%
  stringr::str_trunc(30) %>%
  unique()

oaq_long <- oaq_long %>%
  mutate(name_short = factor(name_short, levels = rev(station_order)))

ggplot(oaq_long, aes(x = pollutant, y = name_short)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = value_norm, fill = value_norm),
    shape = 21, color = "white", alpha = 0.85, na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1, 8), guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette   = "YlOrRd",
    direction = 1,
    na.value  = "grey85",
    name      = "Relative concentration\n(normalised within pollutant)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Multi-pollutant profile: Delhi CPCB stations via OAQ",
    subtitle = "Stations ordered by PM2.5 (top = highest) | Circle size and color = relative concentration",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Live data from OAQ platform | Fetched: ",
      format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M IST")
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 7.5),
    legend.position    = "top",
    plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey40")
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(
    barwidth  = unit(10, "lines"),
    barheight = unit(0.5, "lines")
  ))

ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "fig_oaq5_pollutant_profile.png"), width = 10, height = 9, dpi = 300)
```

---

# Discussion

## What OAQ adds

The OAQ platform supplies three items that the historical CPCB data repository
does not supply:

1. Authoritative coordinates in the station metadata. There is no geocoding
   step, no Nominatim fallback, and no missing coordinates.

2. Multi-pollutant readings (PM2.5, PM10, NO2, O3, CO, NOx) from the same
   station at the same timestamp. The historical API returns only PM2.5.

3. Live readings at 15-minute resolution through `oaq_get_station_24h()`. These
   readings make time-of-day analysis and near-real-time assessment of
   monitoring gaps possible.

## Station network agreement

The network comparison map shows that the CPCB historical coordinates (from
`cpcb_add_coords()`) and the OAQ coordinates agree closely for most stations.
Where differences occur, they are small. Their probable cause is the Nominatim
geocoding fallback. `cpcb_add_coords()` uses this fallback for stations that are
temporarily absent from the CPCB live feed. For the gap analysis, we prefer the
OAQ coordinates as the ground truth.

## Temporal caveat

The satellite data is from November 2022, but the OAQ readings are live. Thus,
the comparison in Part 5 is not a strict validation. Seasonal and year-to-year
variation in Delhi PM2.5 can be more than 30%. Because of this variation, the
satellite and ground readings will have different absolute values. The analysis
is most useful for *relative* spatial patterns. These patterns show which wards
have too few monitors, independent of the absolute PM2.5 level.

## Priority wards

The priority map comparison shows that the conclusions of the gap analysis do
not change much with the coordinate source. Most wards that the CPCB historical
analysis classified as "High priority" are also "High priority" in the OAQ
analysis. This result validates the original method.
